P15s1: So early on, members usually need to have more available resource than acute need, and some practical skills to contribute. They usually need to be willing to learn, too.
P22z: Any humane membership process should have ways of not flat-out rejecting people who fall into these categories, or anyone else it can’t take right now, like saying “later” or “in another role.” It could also say “with more support.”
P13p2x: There is a difficult paradox to consider. The need for new members in a small community is greater, but the ability of that community to tolerate the disruption of new members is less. With only eight people in the community, someone still has to grow the food and fix whatever breaks. Somebody has to balance the books and watch the kids, and the water system has to keep working. The water well doesn’t care how beautiful someone’s heart is.

P16k: I still don’t know how to keep this language of capacity from becoming a respectable way to exclude people who are disabled, poor, less articulate, maybe simply uncomfortable or unfamiliar with therapeutic language, or for whatever reason deemed inconvenient. Pretending capacity is unlimited won’t solve that. Any real process would need concrete criteria, and review by someone who wasn’t part of the decision. It would also need a way to revisit a “not now” decision on membership. Even then, the power to veto membership applications based on capacity remains dangerous.
